source.title: HF Hospitalization Risk in T2D Lower With GLP-1RAs Than DPP-4 Inhibitors, Similar With SGLT-2 Inhibitors
source.source_type: society journal scan / secondary clinical evidence summary

cited_primary_article.authors_as_printed: Xu Y, Huang T, Zhang Y, et al.
cited_primary_article.title: Risk of Heart Failure Hospitalization for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus DPP-4 Inhibitors or SGLT-2 Inhibitors in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Target Trial Emulation

extraction_metadata.source_boundary: Atoms describe what the ACC journal scan reports. Results from the cited Circulation study remain secondary reports and are not represented as if the ACC summary generated participant data.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACC journal scan reports that, in patients with type 2 diabetes, hospitalization for heart failure was lower with GLP-1 receptor agonists than with DPP-4 inhibitors and similar with SGLT-2 inhibitors in two real-world target trial emulations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D), the risk of hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) was significantly lower with GLP-1RAs than DPP-4 inhibitors while it was similar compared with SGLT-2 inhibitors

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACC journal scan reports that Xu and colleagues used SCREAM population data from Sweden to conduct two emulated trials comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists with DPP-4 inhibitors and with SGLT-2 inhibitors.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Using population data on patients with T2D through the SCREAM project (Stockholm Creatinine Measurements) in Sweden, Yang Xu, PhD, et al., conducted two emulation trials

atoms.canonical_statement: The GLP-1 receptor agonists listed in the ACC summary were exenatide, liraglutide, lixisenatide, dulaglutide, and semaglutide.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: GLP-1RAs included were exenatide, liraglutide, lixisenatide, dulaglutide and semaglutide.

exposures.details: Exenatide, liraglutide, lixisenatide, dulaglutide, and semaglutide

atoms.canonical_statement: The DPP-4 inhibitors listed in the ACC summary were sitagliptin, vildagliptin, and linagliptin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: DPP-4 inhibitors were sitagliptin, vildagliptin and linagliptin.

atoms.canonical_statement: The SGLT-2 inhibitors listed in the ACC summary were dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, empagliflozin, and ertugliflozin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SGLT-2 inhibitors were dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, empagliflozin and ertugliflozin.

atoms.canonical_statement: The first emulated trial included 32,979 patients with type 2 diabetes; the median age was 64 years, 40% were women, 42% received a GLP-1 receptor agonist, and 58% received a DPP-4 inhibitor.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In the first trial, with 32,979 patients with T2D (median age 64 years, 40% women), 42% took a GLP-1RA and 58% a DDP-4 inhibitor.

population.label: First emulated trial: patients with type 2 diabetes; median age 64 years; 40% women; 42% received a GLP-1RA and 58% a DPP-4 inhibitor

atoms.canonical_statement: In the first emulated trial, the weighted hospitalization-for-heart-failure incidence rate among GLP-1 receptor agonist users was 12.1 events per 1,000 person-years during 10 to 36 months of follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Over the follow-up of 10-36 months, the weighted incidence rate was 12.1 vs. 15.8 events per 1,000 person-years, respectively

population.label: First emulated trial: patients with type 2 diabetes; median age 64 years; 40% women; 42% received a GLP-1RA and 58% a DPP-4 inhibitor

atoms.canonical_statement: In the first emulated trial, the weighted hospitalization-for-heart-failure incidence rate among DPP-4 inhibitor users was 15.8 events per 1,000 person-years during 10 to 36 months of follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Over the follow-up of 10-36 months, the weighted incidence rate was 12.1 vs. 15.8 events per 1,000 person-years, respectively

atoms.canonical_statement: In the first emulated trial, the three-year absolute hospitalization-for-heart-failure risk was 3.43% with GLP-1 receptor agonists and 4.30% with DPP-4 inhibitors, with a weighted hazard ratio of 0.77.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the three-year absolute HHF risk was 3.43% vs. 4.30% (weighted hazard ratio [HR], 0.77).

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Three-year absolute HHF risk 3.43% vs. 4.30%; weighted HR 0.77.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACC summary reports that the absolute hospitalization-for-heart-failure risk difference was largest among patients with higher predicted baseline heart-failure risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the absolute risk difference was largest among patients with a higher predicted risk of HF at baseline.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACC summary reports that findings were consistent across most subgroups, between individual agents, and in per-protocol analyses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Findings were consistent across most subgroups, between single agents and in per-protocol analyses.

atoms.canonical_statement: In positive-control analyses, the three-year absolute risk of major adverse cardiovascular events was 5.49% with GLP-1 receptor agonists and 6.31% with DPP-4 inhibitors, with a weighted hazard ratio of 0.85.

atoms.canonical_statement: The ACC summary reports that roughly 90% of the patient population did not have heart failure.

population.label: Study population; roughly 90% did not have heart failure at baseline

atoms.canonical_statement: The study authors, as quoted by the ACC summary, suggest that GLP-1 receptor agonists could reduce hospitalization-for-heart-failure risk in patients with type 2 diabetes regardless of heart-failure history, addressing both primary and secondary prevention.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: our findings suggest that GLP-1RAs could be used to reduce the risk of HHF in patients with T2D, regardless of [HF] history, thereby addressing both primary and secondary prevention needs
